clauses.text: Never PR a feature branch straight into `main`.
Keep this file current in the same PR.
Never push directly to `main`.
add a `CHANGELOG.md` entry in the same change. A `dev → main` merge with no bump is a no-op release. -
A release is cut by a version bump, not by a merge.
Without `--trap-command` the generated test fails
clauses.rationale: A baseline that only asserts good-input-passes goes green the day someone weakens a checker. Proven on this very skill: stubbing validateSpec to always return ok left the golden green and turned only the trap red.

clauses.text: fails until a real run is frozen
clauses.rationale: The scaffolded baseline test fails on purpose so `ci / <name>` cannot go green on a skill nobody has run. If this becomes a passing placeholder instead, rung 3 degrades from a gate into a promise, and every promise in this repo has eventually been broken by someone in a hurry.

clauses.text: Wait for the answer before asking the next
clauses.rationale: A batch of questions is a form. The spec is a conversation whose later questions depend on the earlier answers, and asking them all at once produces a spec assembled from defaults nobody chose.

clauses.text: Never overwrite an existing skill
clauses.rationale: A skills/<name> directory that already exists is far more likely to be someone's work than a mistake. Overwriting one destroys uncommitted work with no diff shown and no undo.

clauses.text: never silently proceed as though it made no difference
clauses.rationale: The spec, the one rule and the split are judgment. A weaker model produces a skill that passes every lint in this repo and is still bad — a failure mode with no automated detector, which is why it has to be surfaced to the user instead.

clauses.text: Never open a PR into `main`
clauses.rationale: The only path to main is a dev -> main promotion. A feature PR against main bypasses the integration branch and, because releases here are publish-on-merge, can cut a tag from an unreviewed state.

clauses.text: an unresolvable anchor aborts before the first byte is written
clauses.rationale: A half-applied wiring is worse than none, because the half that landed makes the rest look done. `ci / shipflow` sat un-required from the day it was introduced for exactly this reason.

clauses.text: Never call a skill done below rung 3
clauses.rationale: Rungs 0-2 prove the scaffolding is correct, which is not the same as the skill working. Conflating them is exactly the failure this skill was built against, and it is the failure that ships skills with decorative evals.

clauses.text: only takes effect when an admin runs it
clauses.rationale: Editing the contexts array in repo-settings.sh changes a file, not GitHub. A skill whose check is written down but never applied goes green on every PR and gates nothing — the most convincing possible form of a missing gate.

clauses.text: Never weaken a check to get green
clauses.rationale: check-spec and the baseline trap are adversarial on purpose. The moment either is edited to accommodate a failing input, every skill made afterwards inherits a gate that no longer gates. Fix the input.

clauses.text: One script call, not a pipeline.
Report in tables, with named columns.
Never claim a visual result without the artifact.
Never print file contents into the conversation.
Announce the skill once, at the start
Keep the machinery invisible.
Show, don't describe.
Say which rung you reached, and never claim more.
`check-spec` and the baseline trap exist to be argued with, not edited. Fix the input. -

Say which rung you reached. -
